entities.name: questioning the government is increasingly treated as a criminal act.

political criticism is being answered not with facts, explanations or democratic debate, but with police notices, multiple FIRs, midnight arrests, interstate operations, custodial intimidation, serious non-bailable charges and digital takedowns.
The crackdown began with YSRCP social media activists.
The target is no longer one category of political worker. The target is dissent itself.
What is unfolding is not a series of isolated police excesses.
The same pattern appears across districts and cases.
A politically inconvenient post is identified.
A ruling-party functionary or sympathiser files a complaint.
Police register an FIR, often under provisions disproportionate to the alleged expression.
The speaker is summoned, picked up or arrested.
Phones are seized, families are denied information and arrest records are prepared after custody has begun.
The same content may produce several FIRs in different jurisdictions.
If ordinary provisions do not secure remand, organised-crime, narcotics, extortion, sexual-offence or extraordinary legal provisions are added.
The prosecution then serves two purposes.
It punishes the person who raised the question and supplies the official basis for asking X, Facebook, Instagram or YouTube to restrict the content.
The speaker is criminalised while the speech disappears.
By the time a court intervenes, the arrest, humiliation, financial damage and political warning have already achieved their purpose.
